terra.problem: The text says all the silver found in the two places was given over, not that the buildings were emptied.
The text says Hezekiah gave up all the silver found there, not everything the two places had.
The comparison calls the bill paid in full, but the passage does not say the silver and gold given over met the full demand.
The passage says the three officials went out. It does not say Hezekiah sent them or where he stayed.
Calling the Rabshakeh's assertion a guess adds how he arrived at it. The text does not say.
The explanation repeats the answer in several forms without much of Papa Dorin's voice.
It states that finding the riders is hard and that the Rabshakeh knows it. The passage gives his challenge, not those facts.
The last sentence assigns the Rabshakeh a motive that the text does not give.
The joke about the chapter being shorter makes the way Scripture is written the joke.
Hezekiah is not described as hearing the shout. The Rabshakeh calls out in Hebrew, and the people on the wall are in hearing.
It is not the first thing the Rabshakeh says when he starts shouting. He first calls the people to hear the king of Assyria's word.
The first-person quote is introduced with only 'he says'; the speaker is not identified until after the quote.
The passage does not say who will be in charge of the people in the land to which they are taken.
The first-person question is introduced with only 'He asks'; the Rabshakeh is not identified until after the quote.
Saying the silence took a lot of self-control presents an unspoken inner struggle as fact.
The passage says the people remained silent. It does not say the gates stayed shut or that nobody opened anything.
The text says the officials' clothes were torn, but does not say they tore the clothes themselves.
The explanation is flat and repeats the clothing detail without much of Papa Dorin's voice.
